TabletCrop.dc.html.title: Photos · iPad crop for every shape

phoneNote.text:
Direction: bold and playful. Each countdown's own colour and font lead; the app chrome stays quiet (soft lavender ground, near-black ink).

Home leads with 'Up next', then upcoming cards, then a separate Done section, so past events stop mixing in.

Detail shows one giant number with a unit switcher (Days, Weeks, Sleeps, Hours) instead of five rows of zeros.

The editor keeps a live preview on top and splits the rest into two tabs: Details (name, date, time, repeats, reminders, count in) and Look (photo, gradients, colours, icon, 4 recent fonts plus All fonts).

Search opens on recents, quick filters (This week, December, 2027, Done) and icon shortcuts, plus holiday suggestions to add. Typing highlights the match and lists upcoming first, then done.

settingsNote.text:
Fonts: the phone editor shows your 4 most recent fonts, and 'All fonts' slides up a sheet with all 11, filterable by Clean, Classic and Fun; the iPad editor uses an anchored scroll box with jump links. The picker previews the event's real title and groups fonts into Clean, Classic and Fun. Fonts here are the app's real font files.

Settings keep everything today's app has (sort, theme, app icon, sounds, haptics, notifications, support, about, delete all) and add defaults for new countdowns: unit, reminders and Done section.

iPad settings use a sidebar of categories with a roomy detail pane, so theme and app icon get big visual pickers.

shareNote.text:
Each unit gets its own supporting tiles: Days shows hours/min/sec, Weeks shows weeks + days, Sleeps shows weekends and bedtimes, Hours shows the giant totals.

Share opens a sheet with three formats: Story image, Square image, and a Calendar file (.ics). The image keeps whatever unit you were looking at.

Everything is made on the phone and sent in the message, so sharing needs no backend. The friend gets the image plus a calendar file they can tap to add.

tabletNote.text:
Split view: sidebar filters, a card list and a live detail pane side by side, so tapping a card never leaves the list.

Editor studio: large live preview on the left (card and full-screen), controls on the right.

Wall mode: an always-on board for an iPad on a stand or kitchen counter, the most tablet-only idea here.

widgetNote.text:
Widgets reuse the card look: event colour fill, big Bricolage numeral, title in the event's own font.

Each widget can follow 'Up next' automatically or be pinned to one countdown, and count in days or sleeps.

Lock screen gets circular, rectangular and inline accessories, plus a Live Activity on the day itself that counts down hours and minutes.

Same widgets carry to Android (Glance) and iPad's extra-large size later.

photoNote.text:
Background becomes Colour or Photo in the editor. Pick from your library or a recent photo, darken it so the numbers stay readable, crop it, and choose whether widgets use it too.

On photo countdowns, text flips to white with a soft shadow, and the detail screen goes full-bleed with glassy tiles.

Photos are copied into the app on the phone, so this needs no backend. The photos here are stand-in illustrations.

Look picker: one screen for background and icon. The first tile adds a photo; recent photos, gradients and colours follow, then icons (or none).

Crop: 'All shapes' outlines every place the photo shows (full screen, card or small widget, wide widget). Pick a shape to set its own crop point, or turn on 'Same spot for all' to move them together.

iPad: one screen with the live preview (plus small and wide widget previews), Details (name, date, time, repeats, reminders, unit) and Look (background, photo, icon, font) side by side. The iPad crop shows each shape's actual crop as a live thumbnail, and adds an iPad landscape shape.
